This matrix is my preliminary guide to where relevant BTO policy information is located, how different webpages and sections relate, and how content is presented. Treat it as a source-discovery and completeness checklist, not as an instruction to include every listed policy topic.
Objective: Determine the smallest rights-compliant set of official policy sources necessary to support the approved BTO Buddy MVP, and design the acquisition strategy before any extraction begins.
Tasks:
Reconcile the source-discovery matrix against the approved MVP scope. Review every row's contents and substantive linked resource. Classify each as:
Essential to the MVP.
Supporting or supplementary.
Context only.
Outside the MVP.
Pending clarification.
Preserve the original source references and record the reason for each classification. Do not silently omit relevant conditions or exceptions.
Map the source structure and relationships. For each relevant source, record whether the information appears in:
A main webpage section.
A same-page bookmark or anchor.
An expandable or nested accordion.
An HTML table, including nested tables.
A separate HDB information webpage.
An HDB Flat Portal or other restricted path.
A linked PDF or downloadable document.
An infographic or image.
An embedded YouTube video.
An external website.
Preserve parent-page relationships, anchor references, linked URLs and content formats.
Identify policy dependencies and exceptions. Determine which linked sources contain conditions or exceptions essential to understanding a rule. Distinguish necessary supporting evidence from optional background information.
Review access and licensing restrictions. For each source category, document:
Applicable website Terms of Use.
Relevant robots.txt restrictions.
Copyright and redistribution considerations.
Proposed acquisition method.
Whether local computational analysis is supportable.
Whether GitHub redistribution or transmission to an external LLM provider is permitted, restricted or unresolved.
Do not treat robots.txt as a copyright licence. Do not assume that publicly accessible content is freely redistributable. Where permission cannot be established, explicitly mark it unresolved.
Design the source manifest. Propose a schema containing:
Stable source ID.
Original URL and canonical URL.
Page or document title.
Parent source and linked-source relationship.
Section heading and anchor.
Content type and structural format.
Relevant policy area and applicant category.
Known effective date or unresolved temporal status.
Planned acquisition method.
Retrieval timestamp.
SHA-256 content hash after acquisition.
Permission status.
Manual review status.
Review non-text resources.
Identify PDFs containing unique MVP-critical policy information.
Identify infographics relevant to HFE preparation or next steps.
Determine whether infographics are supplementary visuals or contain unique policy facts.
Record YouTube videos as references unless they contain unique essential information.
Do not assume that images or videos may be downloaded or embedded.
Design the corpus strategy. Distinguish:
Local original HTML and permitted source snapshots.
Local processed passages and indexes containing source text.
Independently authored, source-attributed policy facts and rule representations suitable for reviewer access after rights review.
Explain how the reviewer-facing corpus can support the approved MVP without unauthorised redistribution.
Address clean-machine reproducibility. Propose how reviewers can run the application from the README without depending on unavailable private files. Do not claim that downloading live webpages later reproduces an identical historical frozen corpus.
Identify source and policy coverage gaps. Flag missing documents, incomplete policy exceptions, unclear effective dates, potentially inaccessible content and other blockers.
Recommend the final acquisition scope. Propose the minimum source list needed to cover:
First-timer couple household composition.
Broad BTO application requirements.
HFE prerequisites, timing and documentation.
Missing applicant information.
Limited, source-verified first-timer and priority considerations.
Limited, source-verified application and non-selection consequences.
Loans and grants remain context-only. Do not expand into financial calculations, detailed financing or unrelated applicant categories.
Deliverables:
A reconciled source-discovery matrix.
An MVP source coverage matrix.
A source relationship and link classification inventory.
A source manifest schema.
A documented rights and access assessment.
A proposed extraction method for each approved source.
A reviewer-reproducibility strategy.
A list of unresolved risks, exclusions and approval decisions.
Map relevant outputs to the project requirement IDs and record proposed decisions.
Stop condition: Do not download, scrape, extract or modify external source content. Do not expand the MVP until I have reviewed and approved the source list, permissions assessment and acquisition plan.

17	## 2. Final revised idea — REQ-PRB-010 (APPROVED) [APP p.1–2]
18	
19	- BTO applicants face a **sequence of decisions**:
20	  - applicant eligibility;
21	  - household composition;
22	  - income;
23	  - HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter requirements;
24	  - priority schemes;
25	  - application consequences.
26	- The problem is **not** that official information is missing. Applicants struggle to work
27	  out which rules apply to *their* circumstances, and what information they still need
28	  before they proceed.
29	- Official tools already exist: HFE assessments, eligibility guidance and application
30	  information. BTO Buddy adds a **pre-application preparation layer** that helps applicants:
31	  - understand the relevant published rules;
32	  - identify missing information;
33	  - prepare questions before they use the official application process.
34	- **Differentiation:** transparency and preparation. BTO Buddy does not replace the
35	  authoritative assessment.
36	
37	### 2.1 Observed gap in existing channels [APP p.1–2] (developer observation)
38	
39	**The HDB website's virtual assistant.**
40	- A screenshot in the project approach shows a test query: a first-timer with four previous
41	  unsuccessful BTO attempts asks whether they have an advantage at the next attempt.
42	- The assistant replied that it did not understand and asked the user to rephrase. It then
43	  listed three generic links:
44	  - a First-Timer (Parents & Married Couples) priority-scheme page on an external
45	    government services directory;
46	  - "Application for a New Flat";
47	  - "Modes of Sale".
48	- The user is left to read through the linked pages themselves.
49	
50	**The website itself.**
51	- Pages link to anchors on the same page, to other portal pages, or to external resources
52	  such as PDFs and other sites.
53	- Information relevant to one user group is scattered across pages, and irrelevant content
54	  is still shown, so important clauses are easy to miss unless every expandable section is
55	  opened.
56	- Some content exists only in infographics (images) or in videos hosted on YouTube.
57	- An applicant may qualify for several schemes without realising it. The site works more as
58	  an **information dump** than as applicant-centred guidance.
59	
60	**Effect on users:** a generic, non-personalised experience that causes fatigue.
61	
62	### 2.2 Potential downstream benefit — HYPOTHESIS ONLY (REQ-PRB-015) [APP p.2]
63	Better-prepared citizens *could* reduce HDB operational load: fewer hotline enquiries and
64	fewer ineligible applications to process. This needs future user testing to validate and
65	quantify, and must not be claimed as a result.
66	
67	## 3. Problem statement — REQ-PRB-011 (APPROVED) [APP p.3]
68	> BTO applicants must navigate multiple interdependent eligibility and application rules.
69	> While authoritative guidance exists, translating these rules into personalised, actionable
70	> preparation steps can require substantial manual interpretation. BTO Buddy aims to reduce
71	> that burden while keeping official sources and human verification central to the process.
72	
73	*(This is the developer's own text; "bto-buddy" is normalised to "BTO Buddy" per D-002.)*
74

76	> Can a hybrid AI assistant combining structured applicant profiling, authoritative policy

78	> a conventional LLM assistant?

- adds proposed decisions D-044 to D-055 to [decisions.md](docs/decisions.md);

- updates the INDEX, the matrix pointer in 02 and the development log.

The anonymity and copied-text scans on the changed files came back clean.

**What I found:**
- **Minimum set: the 4 seed pages.** They cover all four Core areas, FT(PMC)/FPPS and cancellation. Priority Schemes (Family Care Scheme sections only) and Modes of Sale (BTO section only) are optional supporting pages. The two HFE guidance PDFs are needed only if the income-guidelines page doesn't list documents by employment type.
- **Non-selection depends on one missing source.** "Exceptions and waivers" has no URL. If it can't be found and verified, I propose cutting that area down to identify-and-link plus a stated evidence gap (D-048).
- **HFE timing may exist only in an infographic.** The 30-day window and processing time may appear only in an image. I recommend treating that as an evidence gap, which also gives a real extraction-gap test case (D-051).
- **First-timer definition not located yet.** It's needed for FT(PMC)/FPPS and the prior-ownership field; I expect it on the Couples and Families page.

**Conflicts I need you to decide:**
1. **PDF tool (D-052).** The approved PDF method (REQ-SRC-009) names PyMuPDF, but the approved dependency list (D-036/D-042) excludes it, and it's AGPL-licensed. I recommend no new dependency: check whether the HTML already carries the content, then validate at most two short PDFs by hand.
2. **Source text and external models (D-054).** If I read the extracted source text to help write facts, that text goes to my model provider. Whether the copyright exception allows that is unresolved. I recommend that you draft the facts from the private passages and I work only on your drafts.

**Your approvals, in order:**
1. **D-044 to D-055.** Most are straightforward:
   - D-045: the BTO-process row's main source is the Application page.
   - D-046: the SC+SPR premium and the resale levy are out of scope, link only.
   - D-047: a non-resident partner is treated as an out-of-scope household.
   - D-049: strip the `si=` tracking parameter from video URLs.
   - D-050: no experiment on the private corpus.

3. **Capturing the 4 seed pages.**

The search turned up the statutory structure and commentary, but not the full text of the five conditions in section 244(2).

- **Basic rule:** Under section 244(1), making a copy of a work or a protected performance recording is a permitted use if the conditions in subsection (2) are met. 244.—(1) If the conditions in subsection (2) are met, it is a permitted use for a person (X) to make a copy of any of the following material
- **Purpose condition:** The copy must be made for computational data analysis or for preparing the material for it. the copy is made for the purpose of —(i) computational data analysis; or (ii) preparing the work or recording for computational data analysis
- **Use and sharing limits:** The copier may not use the copy for other purposes, and may share it only to verify results or for collaborative research related to the analysis. X does not use the copy for any other purpose
- **Lawful access:** Commentary says section 244(2)(d) covers lawful access and gives examples. Copyright Act 2021 S244(2)(d) provides illustrations of what "lawful access" means. "For example, if certain material can only be accessed through a paid subscription, the user cannot circumvent the paywall to access the material." A second example from the same source is that a user cannot gain access to material that is placed on a database by breaching the terms of use of the database.
- **Definition:** Section 243 defines "computational data analysis" to include using a computer program to identify, extract and analyse information or data from the work, and using the work as an example to improve a program's functioning. "(a) using a computer program to identify, extract and analyze information or data from the work or recording; and (b) using the work or recording as an example of a type of information or data to improve the functioning of a computer program in relation to that type of information or data."
- **Contract override:** One commentary states that neither can it be eliminated from nor modified in a contract.

Caveat: these are secondary sources, not the statute itself. The Reed Smith article is the only one that says section 244(2) sets out five conditions, and none of the results lists all five. Check the official text on Singapore Statutes Online before relying on the exact wording of any condition.

<details><summary>Tool result</summary>

```
Section 244 creates a permitted use allowing a person (X) to copy a work or a recording of a protected performance for computational data analysis (CDA). Under s 244(1), this applies only if the conditions in subsection (2) are met. Under s 244(3), "making a copy" includes storing or retaining it.

**The conditions in s 244(2)**

- **(a) Purpose:** The copy must be made for CDA, or to prepare the work or recording for CDA.
- **(b) No other use:** X must not use the copy for any other purpose.
- **(c) Limited supply:** X must not supply the copy to anyone, by communication or otherwise, except:
  - (i) to verify the results of the CDA X carried out, or
  - (ii) for collaborative research or study related to that CDA.
- **(d) Lawful access:** X must have lawful access to the source copy (the "first copy") from which the copy is made. The illustrations clarify this:
  - Access obtained by circumventing paywalls is not lawful access.
  - Access obtained in breach of a database's terms of use is not lawful access. Terms that are void under s 187 are disregarded.
- **(e) Status of the first copy:** One of three alternatives must apply:
  - (i) the first copy is not an infringing copy;
  - (ii) it is infringing, but X did not know this. If it came from a flagrantly infringing online location (whether or not that location is subject to an access-disabling order under s 325), X also neither knew nor could reasonably have known;
  - (iii) it is infringing, but using infringing copies is necessary for a "prescribed purpose," and X uses the copy only for CDA. The page does not say what the prescribed purposes are, so you would need the regulations.

**Related subsections**

- **Subsection (4):** X may communicate the work or recording to the public if the communication uses a copy made under subsection (1), and the same supply limits as in (2)(c) apply.
- **Subsection (5):** Supplying copies under this section is not treated as publishing the material. Such supply is also disregarded when determining the duration of copyright.

This is a summary of the text on the page, not legal advice. The page notes that later amendments may not be reflected, so check the official text on Singapore Statutes Online.
```

<details><summary>Tool result</summary>

```
**Section 187 (Copyright Act 2021)** makes certain contract terms void if they try to take away specified permitted uses.

**Permitted uses covered (s 187(1))**

A contract term is void to the extent it purports, directly or indirectly, to "exclude or restrict" any permitted use under:

- **Division 6 (public collections)**, except s 234, which covers supplying copies of published literary, dramatic or musical works or articles between libraries and archives.
- **Division 7 (computer programs)**.
- **Division 8 (computational data analysis)**. This division comprises ss 243–244, so **s 244 is included**. The page does not reproduce s 244's text, so this answer does not describe what it permits.
- **Division 17 (judicial proceedings and legal advice)**.

Permitted uses under other divisions, such as Division 2 (fair uses) and Division 3 (education), are not listed in this section.

**Specific acts (s 187(2))**

Without limiting subsection (1), a contract term is void to the extent it prevents or restricts these acts, where they constitute a permitted use under the provisions above:

- making a copy of a work or a recording of a protected performance;
- supplying a copy of a work or a recording of a performance, by communication or otherwise;
- performing a work or a recording of a protected performance.

**Timing (s 187(3))**

The section applies to contracts made before, on or after 21 November 2021.

**Effect**

The offending term is void, but only to the extent it excludes or restricts the protected permitted use. The page does not address what happens to the rest of the contract.
```

### Claude · 2026-10-28 08:59:53

## D-047: I recommend reversing it

My first draft was wrong. D-033 puts any **first-timer couple (married or engaged)** in scope and doesn't exclude a couple because of citizenship. Treating an SC with a non-resident spouse or fiancé(e) as out of scope would have quietly cut Core scope. Which citizenship combination a couple has is itself one of the household-composition rules the assistant has to explain.

The revised D-047 (still proposed) says:
- **In scope:** SC + non-resident couples, with facts written only from the couple rows of the "families with non-residents" section of Couples and Families, and only where the conditions are explicit.
- **Fallback:** if those conditions turn out to be discretionary or too detailed to verify, the assistant names the situation, redirects to HDB and states an evidence gap.
- **Still out of scope:** non-resident parent or child households.
- **Unmatched combinations:** any citizenship combination with no matching section gets an evidence gap, never a determination.

It needs no extra capture, because that section is on a seed page.

## Rights check results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| HDB robots.txt | All 4 seed pages, Priority Schemes, Modes of Sale and the PDF media path are **allowed**. `/hdb-flat-portal` is **disallowed**, which covers the HFE FAQ page, so I won't fetch it by any automated means. There's no crawl delay |
| HDB bot protection | Both curl and headless Chromium got **HTTP 403**, even with an honest user agent. The error pages are saved privately as evidence, with hashes |
| HDB Terms of Use | **Not read, still unresolved.** The page text loads with JavaScript, and the browser attempt got 403. HDB's terms for its separate mynicehome site limit use to personal, non-commercial purposes. That's a different site, so I haven't assumed the same terms apply |
| Copyright Act s 244 | It allows local copies made for computational analysis, on four conditions: no other use; no supply to others except to verify results or for collaborative research; **lawful access**; and a non-infringing source. Accessing in breach of terms of use isn't lawful access, unless s 187 voids the term. I read this from a secondary source because the official statutes site returned 403 |
| Copyright Act s 187 | Contract terms that restrict this exception are void |

What this means for the project:
- **Private corpus:** keeping local copies for analysis is plausible under s 244.
- **GitHub:** committing the copies is not covered by s 244.
- **LLM providers:** sending source text to a provider counts as supplying a copy to a third party, so that's ruled out as well. This firms up D-054.

## Capture: you should capture the seed pages manually

I can't capture them in line with the provenance rules. HDB actively blocks automated clients. The only way around that is to disguise the client, and that is ethically wrong. It would also undermine "lawful access", which is the basis for keeping local copies. A normal visit in your browser is plain public access, and the manual rendered-DOM method was approved from the start (REQ-SRC-006). I've revised D-055 to make it the main method.

For each of the 4 seed pages:
1. Open it in Chrome, not logged in, and click every accordion open.
2. Open DevTools → Console and run `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)`. This copies the page as currently shown, with the accordions open, and no images.
3. Paste it into `data/private_corpus/raw/S01/<UTC timestamp>.html`. Use S02 for the HFE page, S03 for Income Guidelines and S04 for Application for a New Flat.
4. Note the time and how many accordions you opened.

Don't use Chrome's "Save as… Complete" or a single-file save. Both would also save the infographic images.

I'll then write `scripts/register_snapshot.py`, which runs offline. For each file it records the hash and timestamp in the manifest, counts open vs closed sections as the completeness check, and splits the text into structured passages, all without network access. It prints only IDs, counts and hashes, so no source text reaches me.

**What I need from you:**
1. Read the HDB Terms of Use in your browser. Save that page and robots.txt the same way into `data/private_corpus/raw/rights/`, so I can summarise the terms and hash both files. Tell me first if the terms forbid copying or automated analysis.
2. Approve D-044 to D-055, including the revised D-047 and D-055.
3. Then do the 4 captures above.

The changes are in [source_acquisition_plan.md](docs/source_acquisition_plan.md) (§7.2a, §10, S01.e), [decisions.md](docs/decisions.md) and the [development log](docs/development_log.md). The private files are git-ignored, and the anonymity scan is clean.

Sources:

### Claude · 2026-10-28 09:07:54

Opening one section closing another usually doesn't stop a single capture. Many accordions only hide the closed sections, and the text stays in the page. Check that first: if it's true, one copy per page captures everything. If not, a console script can open each section in turn and save them all into one file.

I couldn't test either script, because HDB blocks me (HTTP 403). The selectors are written for standard accessible accordions, so you may need to adjust them.

### Step 1: Check whether closed sections are still in the page (read-only, per page)

Paste this in DevTools → Console. It doesn't click anything.

```js
(() => {
  const main = document.querySelector('main') || document.body;
  const btns = [...main.querySelectorAll('[aria-expanded]')];
  console.table(btns.map((b, i) => {
    const id = b.getAttribute('aria-controls');
    const panel = id ? document.getElementById(id) : b.nextElementSibling;
    return { i, heading: b.textContent.trim().slice(0, 60), expanded: b.getAttribute('aria-expanded'),
             panelInDom: !!panel, panelTextLen: panel ? panel.textContent.trim().length : 0 };
  }));
  const nd = document.getElementById('__NEXT_DATA__');
  console.log('controls:', btns.length, '| <details>:', main.querySelectorAll('details').length,
              '| __NEXT_DATA__ chars:', nd ? nd.textContent.length : 'absent');
})();
```

How to read the output:
- **Every row has `panelTextLen` > 0, including collapsed ones:** the content is in the page. One `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)` per page is complete, and you're done.
- **Collapsed rows show 0 or `panelInDom: false`:** those sections are removed from the page while closed. Go to step 2.
- **`controls: 0`:** the accordions don't use standard attributes. Send me the output and I'll adapt the selectors.
- **`__NEXT_DATA__` present and large:** the site may embed all page content as JSON, closed sections included. It's captured by the same copy, and I'll use it offline as a cross-check.

The output contains only headings and counts, so you can paste it back to me without sharing source text.

### Step 2 (only if needed): Collect sections one at a time

This script opens each section in turn, about one per second. It saves each heading and section into one file together with the full page. It also opens parent sections first, so nested accordions are reached.

```js
(async () => {
  const sleep = ms => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms));
  const main = document.querySelector('main') || document.body;
  const panelOf = b => { const id = b.getAttribute('aria-controls');
                         return id ? document.getElementById(id) : b.nextElementSibling; };
  const openAncestors = async b => {           // nested accordions: reopen the parent first
    for (const p of [...main.querySelectorAll('[aria-expanded="false"]')])
      if (p !== b && panelOf(p)?.contains(b)) { p.click(); await sleep(1000); }
  };
  const seen = new Set(), sections = [];
  for (let pass = 0, found = true; found && pass < 5; pass++) {   // re-scan for nested ones
    found = false;
    for (const b of [...main.querySelectorAll('[aria-expanded]')]) {
      const key = b.id || b.textContent.trim();
      if (seen.has(key)) continue; seen.add(key); found = true;
      await openAncestors(b);
      if (b.getAttribute('aria-expanded') !== 'true') { b.click(); await sleep(1000); }
      const panel = panelOf(b);
      sections.push({ order: sections.length, heading: b.textContent.trim(),
                      expanded: b.getAttribute('aria-expanded'), panel_html: panel ? panel.outerHTML : null });
    }
  }
  copy(JSON.stringify({ url: location.href, captured_at: new Date().toISOString(),
                        user_agent: navigator.userAgent, page_html: document.documentElement.outerHTML, sections }));
  console.log('sections:', sections.length, '| empty:', sections.filter(s => !s.panel_html?.trim()).length,
              '| not expanded:', sections.filter(s => s.expanded !== 'true').length);
})();
```

Save the copied result as `data/private_corpus/raw/S0n/<UTC timestamp>.json`.

The capture is complete when:
- the section count equals the control count from step 1;
- the empty count is 0;
- the not-expanded count is 0.

If any count is off, send me the console line. It contains only numbers.

### Why this approach
- **It's still manual capture.** The script runs in your own normal browser session, at about human clicking speed, on one page you opened yourself. Nothing gets around the bot protection, and nothing follows links. I've recorded it in [plan §10](docs/source_acquisition_plan.md) as manual rendered-DOM capture with sequential console-assisted expansion, so it's disclosed.
- **No images are saved.** The file holds only the page structure: image links and alt text, not the infographic files.
- **Nothing is assembled by hand.** Keeping each section with its own heading avoids misattributing a condition to the wrong applicant group (REQ-SRC-003).
- **Clicking each section and saving separately also works.** It just means about 15 files and is easier to get wrong, so I'd only fall back to it if the script misbehaves.

Once the files are in place, I'll write the offline `register_snapshot.py`. For each file it records the hash and timestamp in the manifest, runs the completeness counts and splits the content into structured passages. It prints only IDs, counts and hashes, never source text.

The real risk is content that only loads when you click, and the procedure below tests for exactly that.

## Procedure for each of the 4 pages

**A. Default copy.** Load the page fresh, not logged in, and wait until it finishes loading. Run the step 1 script and paste the table to me. Then run:
```js
copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)
```
Save it as `data/private_corpus/raw/S0n/<UTC timestamp>_default.html`.

**B. Expanded copy.** In the same tab, open everything you can see that expands, including nested sections like FT(PMC) and FPPS and any "read more" links. Order doesn't matter, and it's fine that they close each other. Scroll to the bottom, run the same `copy(...)` and save it as `S0n/<UTC timestamp>_expanded.html`.

**C. Note anything shown on the page about when it was last updated or reviewed.** That's the only date evidence we'll have for D-021.

| Folder | Page |
|---|---|
| S01 | Couples and Families |
| S02 | HFE letter |
| S03 | Income Guidelines and Documents |
| S04 | Application for a New Flat (make sure "Cancellation of flat application" is opened) |

## How completeness gets proven

Once the files are saved, my offline script compares each page's two copies. Text that appears only in the expanded copy would mean some content loads only on click. In that case, we use the step 2 collector for that page only. If there's no such text, the default copy is complete and both files are kept, with hashes.

The script also checks, for each page:
- the visible page text against the embedded page data, to catch content that's only in the data;
- that each section on the expected list is present, such as FT(PMC), FPPS, the under-21 fiancé(e) note, the HFE validity section and the cancellation section.

It prints only yes/no results, counts and hashes, so no source text reaches me.

Two copies per page is a few extra minutes, and it turns "we think we captured everything" into a measured result for the accordion-coverage check (REQ-SRC-012).

If you want, I'll write `scripts/register_snapshot.py` (offline, standard library only) while you capture, so it's ready when the files land.

# Structure-only probe: prints labels, paths, counts. Never prints source passages.
import json, re, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
from audit_snapshots import Snapshot, norm, strip_html, json_strings, short, SKIP_TAGS, HEADING_TAGS
from pathlib import Path

class Sectioned(Snapshot):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(); self.cur = "(top)"; self.buckets = {}
    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        n = len(self.headings) + len(self.toggles)
        super().handle_endtag(tag)
        if len(self.headings) + len(self.toggles) > n:
            lab = (self.headings[-1][1] if len(self.headings) and tag in HEADING_TAGS else self.toggles[-1][1])
            self.cur = short(lab)
    def handle_data(self, data):
        super().handle_data(data)
        if not self._skip and not self._in_next:
            self.buckets.setdefault(self.cur, []).append(data)

PROBES = {

         "first_timer": r"first-timer|first timer", "below_21": r"below 21", "non_resident_spouse": r"non-resident spouse",
         "solemnis": r"solemnis", "income_ceiling": r"income ceiling"},
 "S02": {"30_days": r"30 (calendar )?days", "9_months": r"\b9 months\b", "processing": r"\b1 month\b|one month|processing time|working days",

         "first_timer": r"first-timer|first timer", "second_timer": r"second-timer|second timer", "fewer_flats": r"fewer|or less|or fewer",
         "exception_variants": r"exception|except|unless|does not apply"},
}
root = Path("data/private_corpus/raw")
for sid, probes in PROBES.items():
    f = next((root / sid).glob("*.html"))
    raw = f.read_text(errors="replace"); s = Sectioned(); s.feed(raw)
    print(f"\n=== {sid}")
    for name, rx in probes.items():
        where = {}
        for lab, parts in s.buckets.items():
            n = len(re.findall(rx, norm(" ".join(parts))))
            if n: where[lab] = n
        nd = len(re.findall(rx, norm(s.next_data)))
        print(f"  {name}: dom_by_section={where} | in_NEXT_DATA_raw={nd}")
    # not-rendered page-data sentences: component name + field + length only
    data = json.loads(s.next_data); dom = norm(" ".join(s.text))
    def comp(path):
        node = data
        for tok in re.findall(r"\.([^.\[]+)|\[(\d+)\]", path)[:-1]:
            k = tok[0] if tok[0] else int(tok[1])
            try: node = node[k]
            except Exception: break
            if isinstance(node, dict) and "componentName" in node: last = node["componentName"]
        return locals().get("last", "-")
    for path, val in json_strings(data):
        if len(val) < 40 or val.startswith(("http", "/", "{")): continue
        txt = norm(strip_html(val) if "<" in val else val)
        miss = [x for x in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?:;])\s+", txt) if len(x) >= 30 and x not in dom]
        if miss:
            print(f"  NOT RENDERED: component={comp(path)} field=…{path[-45:]} sentences={len(miss)} chars={sum(map(len,miss))}")
    if sid == "S03":
        for h in s.links:
            if re.search(r"\.pdf|guide|go\.gov\.sg", h, re.I): print("  guide/pdf link:", short(h))

Every item that doesn't appear is metadata: page descriptions and descriptions of link cards to other pages.
- **All content accordions are present.** That's 5 each on S01, S02 and S04; S03 has none. The four unlabelled toggles on the HFE page appear on every page, so they're site navigation, not content.

| Core area | Status |
|---|---|
| Household composition | Covered. Fiancé(e) and married-couple sections, the non-resident spouse section (relevant to D-047), the under-21 note, the no-change-of-persons note, core family nucleus, and property ownership |
| Broad application requirements | Covered: sales launch, ballot, application fee and the valid-HFE requirement (S04) |
| HFE prerequisites and timing | Covered. The 30-day window, 9-month validity and processing time **are in the page text**, so the gap I expected (only in the infographic) doesn't exist |
| HFE documents | **Partly covered.** The Documents section on S03 doesn't break documents down by employment type. That detail only appears in the two linked guides, which now link through `go.gov.sg/hfe-employment-status-guide` and `go.gov.sg/hfe-income-declaration-guide` |

The Limited areas:
- **Non-selection:** covered. The waiver, fewer-flats and second-timer wording all sits inside the "Cancellation of flat application" section, so the separate "exceptions and waivers" source was never a separate page.
- **FT(PMC) and FPPS:** **not on the Couples and Families page at all.** They're absent from both the visible page and its embedded data, so the matrix is out of date for that page, which HDB last updated on 23 Aug 2026. The Application page has a "Priority schemes" section pointing elsewhere, so they're now most likely on the **Priority Schemes page**.

These checks only confirm that the right topics are present. They don't verify any policy content; that happens when facts are written from the pages.

### Claude · 2026-10-28 10:28:37

## 1. The Priority Schemes page doesn't expand scope

Capturing it doesn't expand scope, because it supplies evidence for an area that's already approved. "Relevant first-timer and priority considerations" is an approved Limited-tier area under D-008. The audit showed FT(PMC) and FPPS are no longer on Couples and Families, so the Priority Schemes page is now the only source for that area. It was also already in your source-discovery matrix as S05, with this same URL.

I'd call it an **approved Essential source** rather than a **seed**. "Seed" refers to the four starting pages recorded in REQ-SRC-001 and D-007, and relabelling it would blur that record. I've moved S05 into the first capture group in both the plan and the proposed D-044.

The scope limits stay as they are:
- **Write facts only** from the FT(PMC), FPPS and Family Care Scheme sections. The other schemes (Third Child, Senior and Tenants' Priority) are captured with the page but are outside the MVP.
- **Limited tier means** identifying the considerations and linking to them, with conditions stated only where they're explicit and verified. It never predicts allocation or ballot outcomes.

To capture it, use the same method as before:
1. Run the step 1 check.
2. Copy the page with `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)`.
3. Save it as `data/private_corpus/raw/S05/<UTC timestamp>_priority_schemes_default.html`.

If you save it without the timestamp, I'll add it from the file's creation time as before.

## 2. Put the PDFs in the raw folder, one folder per source

Like the HTML pages, the PDFs are acquired source copies, so they belong in `raw/`, which is git-ignored:

```
data/private_corpus/raw/S07/<UTC timestamp>_hfe-employment-status-guide.pdf
data/private_corpus/raw/S08/<UTC timestamp>_hfe-income-declaration-guide.pdf
```

- **Don't open and re-save them.** Keep the files exactly as downloaded so the hash matches what HDB served.
- **Note the final URL** from your browser's download list. The page links to a `go.gov.sg/...` short link, and the manifest needs both that link and the address it redirected to (probably on `file.go.gov.sg`).
- **Note any date printed on the PDF**, such as a publication or version date. It's the only effective-date evidence these files will have.

Once they're in place, I'll record the hashes and timestamps. Under D-052 I won't parse the PDFs with a new library, and under D-054 I won't read their text. You check the relevant pages by hand when writing the HFE-document facts.

### Claude · 2026-10-28 10:36:48

Now the script that fills in the acquisition fields from the raw files:

**Tool call: Write**

```
{
 "file_path": "<repo>/scripts/register_snapshots.py",
 "content": "\"\"\"Fill acquisition provenance in data/sources_manifest.json from private raw captures.\n\nFor each `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/<UTC>_<name>.(html|pdf)` it records:\n- retrieved_at, parsed from the UTC prefix, which is the file's creation time at save;\n- raw_sha256, byte_size and private_path;\n- text_sha256 for HTML (normalised DOM text, via audit_snapshots). This hash detects real\n  content drift on a later re-capture without storing any text.\n\nOnly metadata is written. The manifest is tracked; the raw files stay Git-ignored (D-005).\nIf a source has several captures, the newest one is registered (REQ-LIC-016). Earlier hashes\nstay in Git history.\n\nUsage: python -I scripts/register_snapshots.py\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport re\nfrom datetime import UTC, datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom audit_snapshots import Snapshot, norm\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nRAW = ROOT / \"data\" / \"private_corpus\" / \"raw\"\nMANIFEST = ROOT / \"data\" / \"sources_manifest.json\"\nSTAMP = re.compile(r\"^(\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}T\\d{6}Z)_\")\n\n\ndef text_hash(html: bytes) -> str:\n    snap = Snapshot()\n    snap.feed(html.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\"))\n    return hashlib.sha256(norm(\" \".join(snap.text)).encode()).hexdigest()\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    manifest = json.loads(MANIFEST.read_text())\n    by_id = {s[\"source_id\"]: s for s in manifest[\"sources\"]}\n    for folder in sorted(p for p in RAW.glob(\"S*\") if p.is_dir()):\n        files = sorted(f for f in folder.iterdir() if STAMP.match(f.name))\n        if not files or folder.name not in by_id:\n            print(f\"skip {folder.name}: no stamped file or no manifest entry\")\n            continue\n        f = files[-1]\n        data = f.read_bytes()\n        stamp = STAMP.match(f.name).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n        retrieved = datetime.strptime(stamp, \"%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ\").replace(tzinfo=UTC)\n        acq = by_id[folder.name][\"acquisition\"]\n        acq.update(\n            {\n                \"retrieved_at\": retrieved.isoformat().replace(\"+00:00\", \"Z\"),\n                \"retrieved_at_basis\": \"file creation time at save (UTC filename prefix)\",\n                \"raw_sha256\": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),\n                \"text_sha256\": text_hash(data) if f.suffix == \".html\" else None,\n                \"byte_size\": len(data),\n                \"private_path\": str(f.relative_to(ROOT)),\n            }\n        )\n        print(f\"{folder.name}: {acq['retrieved_at']} sha256={acq['raw_sha256'][:12]} ({f.name})\")\n    MANIFEST.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}
```

Only metadata is written.\n    \"\"\"\n    manifest = json.loads(MANIFEST.read_text())\n    by_id = {s[\"source_id\"]: s for s in manifest[\"sources\"]}\n    for folder in sorted(p for p in RAW.glob(\"S*\") if p.is_dir()):\n        files = sorted(f for f in folder.iterdir() if STAMP.match(f.name))\n        if not files or folder.name not in by_id:\n            print(f\"skip {folder.name}: no stamped file or no manifest entry\")\n            continue\n        f = files[-1]\n        data = f.read_bytes()\n        stamp = STAMP.match(f.name).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n        retrieved = datetime.strptime(stamp, \"%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ\").replace(tzinfo=UTC)\n        text_sha = None\n        if f.suffix == \".html\":\n            snap = Snapshot()\n            snap.feed(data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\"))\n            text_sha = hashlib.sha256(norm(\" \".join(snap.text)).encode()).hexdigest()\n        acq = by_id[folder.name][\"acquisition\"]\n        acq.update(\n            {\n                \"retrieved_at\": retrieved.isoformat().replace(\"+00:00\", \"Z\"),\n                \"retrieved_at_basis\": \"file creation time at save (UTC filename prefix)\",\n                \"raw_sha256\": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),\n                \"text_sha256\": text_sha,\n                \"byte_size\": len(data),\n                \"private_path\": str(f.relative_to(ROOT)),\n            }\n        )\n        print(f\"{folder.name}: {acq['retrieved_at']} sha256={acq['raw_sha256'][:12]} ({f.name})\")\n    MANIFEST.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    command = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else \"\"\n    if command == \"audit\":\n        run_audit()\n    elif command == \"register\":\n        run_register()\n    else:\n        sys.exit(\"usage: python -I scripts/snapshots.py {audit|register}\")"

### Claude · 2026-10-28 10:57:27

The repo is cleaned up, and it now holds only files that are needed or are submission evidence. Ruff, mypy, pytest and the lockfile check all pass, there are no broken doc links, and the anonymity scan is clean.

## What changed
| Item | Action | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/source_acquisition_plan.md` (800 lines) | **Replaced** by [docs/data_sources.md](docs/data_sources.md) (about 350 lines) | The old file was a pre-capture plan, with speculation, superseded automated-capture steps and a copy of the decision list. The new doc describes the current state of the sources only. |
| `scripts/audit_snapshots.py` + `register_snapshots.py` | **Merged** into [scripts/snapshots.py](scripts/snapshots.py) with `audit` and `register` commands | One tool instead of two. It regenerates the manifest byte-for-byte identically, so the recorded hashes stay reproducible. |
| `.DS_Store`, `src/bto_buddy.egg-info`, tool caches, `__pycache__` | **Deleted** | Local leftovers, all git-ignored and regenerated automatically. |
| References in CLAUDE.md, INDEX, 02, 03, decisions and the development log | **Repointed** | No links to the deleted files remain. The development log keeps the history and adds a cleanup entry. |

## What I kept, and why
- **`data_sources.md` as its own doc.** The submission plan explicitly allows separate files for policy-source manifests (REQ-DOC-012). Merging it into decisions.md or the development log would mix reference material with decisions and history, and would bloat both files.
- **`data/sources_manifest.json`.** It's the required provenance record (REQ-SRC-002).
- **`scripts/snapshots.py`.** Without it, the hashes in the manifest couldn't be re-checked.
- **`docs/project_context/` 01–06 and `architecture.md`.** They're the approved requirements and design that every decision cites. Merging them now would break traceability for little gain.
- **`README.md`.** It's still a placeholder, and it becomes the main deliverable later.

Private captures, the rights-check evidence, `references/private/` and `.venv` are all git-ignored. I didn't touch any of them.

## Needs your approval: D-056
The Playwright `capture` dependency group is now unused, because HDB blocks automated access and capture is manual. I've proposed removing it from `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, and removing the planned `capture_sources.py` from the architecture doc. I haven't done it, because it reverses your approved decision D-042. Tell me if I should go ahead.

This is a good point to commit:
- **Files:** `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/`, `data/sources_manifest.json` and `scripts/snapshots.py`. Nothing private is included.
- **Suggested message:** `data: add source manifest, data-sources doc and snapshot tooling`.
- **Push:** fine to the private remote after the secret scan.

**Simplifications versus the recommended structure, with reasons:**

| Recommended item | Change | Reason |
----
- Retrieval is BM25 + aliases + topic filter + rule-linked facts. Propose anything else only
  if dev recall@5 < 0.90 because of paraphrase (D-031).
- **Dependencies are limited to D-036 + D-042** (Playwright, opt-in `capture` group, scripts only). Anything else needs an approved decision.
- Infographics and videos are links in `data/visual_resources.json`, never runtime evidence.
  `docker run --rm -p 8501:8501 --env-file .env bto-buddy`
- Health check: `curl -f http://localhost:8501/_stcore/health`

**Docker image:** two-stage build on `python:3.12-slim`, uv 0.13.6, runs as non-root `app`,
port 8501, HEALTHCHECK on `/_stcore/health`. Configuration comes from environment variables
only. `.dockerignore` keeps `references/`, `data/private_corpus/`, `.env*`, docs, tests and
caches out of the build context.

- Add a dependency with `uv add <pkg>` (or `uv add --dev <pkg>`), with a justification comment
  in `pyproject.toml`. Never hand-edit `uv.lock`.
- Source capture tooling (opt-in, D-042): `uv sync --group capture`, then
  `uv run --group capture playwright install chromium` (once per machine). Run capture only
  with an approved page list.
- Source capture is **manual** (D-055, proposed). HDB returns 403 to automated clients, and
  that block must never be bypassed. The developer saves rendered pages and PDFs to
  `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/<UTC>_<name>`.
- Snapshot audit (offline, prints structure only, never source text):
  `python3 -I scripts/snapshots.py audit`
- Record hashes and timestamps in the manifest: `python3 -I scripts/snapshots.py register`
- Evaluation commands: add them here only after they have been verified.

### Claude · 2026-10-28 13:43:26

**Store the full copy privately, and track only a paraphrased summary plus its hash.** The Terms of Use page is itself HDB's copyrighted content, so it follows the same rules as the policy pages.

| What | Where | Committed? |
|---|---|---|
| Full copy of the page, captured the same way as before (DevTools → `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)`) | `data/private_corpus/raw/rights/<UTC>_hdb_terms_of_use.html` | **No.** Git-ignored, alongside the two 403 block pages already there |
| URL, check time, SHA-256 of the copy, the page's "last updated" date | the `R-HDB-WWW` record in `data/sources_manifest.json` (`terms_url`, `terms_checked_at`, `terms_sha256`) | Yes |
| Your own paraphrase of the clauses that matter, with very short quotes only where the exact wording decides the point | `terms_summary` in the manifest, and the Terms of Use row in [data_sources.md §6.1](docs/data_sources.md) | Yes |
| What the terms mean for this project (local copies, redistribution, LLM use) | [data_sources.md §6.2–6.3](docs/data_sources.md); a decision entry if they change anything | Yes |

**How this keeps it verifiable without redistributing it:**
- Reviewers get the official URL, the date you read it and the hash. They can read the live page themselves, and the hash proves which version your assessment relied on.
- That's the same approach used for the policy pages. Committing the full text would be redistribution, which s 244(2)(c) doesn't cover.

**Clauses to look for when you read it:**
- copyright or IP ownership, and what reuse is allowed (personal, non-commercial, with attribution);
- any ban on automated access, scraping, crawling, data mining or "robots";
- whether reproduction, modification or redistribution is allowed;
- linking terms (the app links to HDB pages);
- disclaimers about accuracy and currency (useful for the README's "not official advice" wording);
- any terms on AI or machine-learning use;
- the "last updated" date.

**The legal significance.** If the terms restrict copying or analysis, s 187 makes those terms void as far as they would block the computational analysis exception. But a breach of the terms could still undermine lawful access under s 244(2)(d), and in practice that depends mainly on how the pages were accessed. Manual browser access with no bypassing of the bot protection is the strongest position. If the terms forbid automated access, that matches the approach you already took.

**Privacy:** HDB's privacy statement covers how HDB handles its own visitors' data. It doesn't govern this project. The project's privacy position rests on using only fictional profiles (REQ-PRIV-001) and on the deployment limitation already recorded, so the privacy statement doesn't need to be stored.

**Who writes the summary.** Reading the terms was part of the rights check you approved, so once you've saved the copy I can read it and draft the paraphrase for you to confirm. If you'd rather no HDB text reached my model provider, read it yourself and give me the key points, and I'll write them up. Either way, I can also extend `snapshots.py register` to fill in the hash and check time automatically from files in `raw/rights/`.

### Claude · 2026-10-28 13:51:45

The capture is complete and enough to finish the rights assessment. The answer is that you can proceed, with two disclosed caveats rather than full clearance: the terms ban copying and linking without HDB's permission. I renamed the file to `raw/rights/2026-10-28T134435Z_hdb_terms_of_use.html`.

**The file and the capture time.** You pasted the terms into the old 403 file, so its creation time (06:19Z) belongs to the old block page. I used its last-modified time instead, 13:44:35Z (21:44 +08:00), which is when you saved the real copy. One side effect: the original 403 evidence file is gone. Its hash stays recorded in [data_sources.md](docs/data_sources.md), which is enough.

**What the terms say, and where each point lands:**

| Clause | Effect |
|---|---|
| **No copying or reuse "for commercial or any other purpose" without HDB's written permission.** There's no research or personal-use exception | The terms alone would forbid even your private copies. Those rest on **Copyright Act s 244**, and **s 187** makes contract terms void where they restrict that exception. Committing copies or sending source text to an LLM was already banned, so the project is consistent with the clause |
| **Written permission needed before linking to, caching or framing the site** | This **conflicts with REQ-ARC-009**, which requires answers to link to HDB pages. I've proposed **D-057** for it (below) |
| **No interfering, overloading, probing, or breaching security measures** | Supports the decision not to get around the bot protection. Your one-page-at-a-time manual access complies |
| **No clause on robots, scraping, data mining or AI** | Nothing extra applies |
| **Content is general information only and must be verified** | Matches the app's "not official advice" disclaimer |
| **The open data licence applies only to published datasets** | It doesn't cover these pages, so the project claims no licence |
| **Privacy section** | Covers how HDB handles its own users' data, so it doesn't apply to an app that uses only fictional profiles |

**Why it isn't full clearance.** Two risks remain:
- The terms' wording against "adapted" works is broad. Writing facts in independent wording, plus the overlap check, keeps that risk low.
- The linking clause.

Neither blocks a private prototype. I read the statute from a secondary source, and this is the project's own reading, not legal advice.

**D-057 (proposed) handles the linking clause:**
- **Keep the official links.** They're required for the assessment and for verifying facts, and the prototype is private and run only locally.
- **Rely on s 244 and s 187** for the private copies.
- **Disclose both clauses in the README** as remaining contractual risk, and state that a public deployment would need HDB's permission.
- **Optionally, email HDB for written permission.** The terms ask for your identity, the content, why and how you'd use it, and for how long. That's your call, since it's an outward-facing step and a reply is unlikely before the deadline. I can draft it if you want.

**Updated:**
- [data/sources_manifest.json](data/sources_manifest.json): HDB's rights record now has the check time, the hash, the page date (24 Jul 2026) and my summary of the clauses.
- [scripts/snapshots.py](scripts/snapshots.py): `register` now also records the terms file's hash and time.
- [data_sources.md](docs/data_sources.md): §6.1 to 6.3 and §10.
- [decisions.md](docs/decisions.md): proposed D-057.
- 03, the register and the [development log](docs/development_log.md).

The manifest is valid JSON, ruff and the test pass, the terms copy is git-ignored, and the anonymity scan is clean.

**Your decisions:** approve D-057 (and D-044 to D-055, which are still only proposed), and decide whether to email HDB.

Suggested commit, with nothing private included:
```bash
git add data/sources_manifest.json scripts/snapshots.py docs/data_sources.md docs/decisions.md \
  docs/development_log.md docs/project_context/03_data_and_licensing.md docs/project_context/requirements_register.md
git commit -m "docs: record HDB Terms of Use review and propose D-057" -m "Pins the Terms of Use version read (hash, page date 24 Jul 2026) in the manifest with an
authored clause summary. Local copies rest on Copyright Act s 244, with s 187 voiding the
contractual copying ban; the linking-permission clause is handled by proposed D-057.
snapshots.py register now records the terms hash and check time.

4B. Offline Content Processing, Completeness Validation and Frozen Corpus Preparation

Objective: Transform the approved, manually captured HDB source snapshots into a traceable, validated and rights-reviewed knowledge base sufficient for the BTO Buddy MVP.

The purpose is to establish verified coverage of the approved MVP, not to extract every potentially relevant document from the wider HDB website.

Current project state

Phase 2A source discovery, rights review and manual source acquisition have been completed.

Approved HTML and PDF snapshots are stored under data/private_corpus/raw/.

data/sources_manifest.json contains the source inventory, classifications, acquisition metadata and available source hashes.

scripts/snapshots.py provides offline snapshot registration and auditing.

Source-acquisition, rights and licensing decisions are recorded in docs/data_sources.md and docs/decisions.md.

Automated browser capture was not adopted because of HDB's automated-access restrictions.

Do not repeat acquisition, scrape webpages, implement Playwright capture or recreate existing tooling.

Required context

Read only the relevant sections of:

docs/project_context/01_problem_and_scope.md

docs/project_context/02_policy_sources.md

docs/project_context/03_data_and_licensing.md

docs/project_context/04_architecture.md

docs/project_context/requirements_register.md

docs/data_sources.md

docs/decisions.md

Follow the approved Dataset A — Content extraction and Validate completeness and freeze the corpus methodology. Use the manually constructed source-discovery matrix, approved source inventory and approved MVP policy scope as the completeness checklist.

A. Offline content processing

Inventory the existing local HTML and PDF snapshots. Cross-check each against data/sources_manifest.json, including source IDs, acquisition status, hashes, capture dates and documented rights restrictions. Flag missing or inconsistent records without silently modifying approved metadata.

Reuse scripts/snapshots.py for existing snapshot registration and structural auditing. Extend it only where necessary; avoid duplicating its responsibilities in new scripts.

Implement an offline extraction pipeline using BeautifulSoup or another justified lightweight parser. Preserve:

Source and section hierarchy.

Headings, paragraphs, lists and tables.

Conditions, exceptions, qualifications and exclusions.

Same-page anchors, hyperlinks and source relationships.

Applicant categories and policy applicability.

Relevant dates and source metadata.

Preserve enough contextual information to prevent conditions or exceptions from being attributed to the wrong applicant category. Avoid arbitrary chunking that separates a rule from its qualifications.

Generate stable source and passage identifiers linked to the existing manifest. Preserve original/canonical URLs, section references, content types, capture timestamps, hashes and known effective dates.

Process existing approved local PDFs only where they contain unique, MVP-relevant information. Preserve page references and manually validate important conditions, dates and numerical values. Do not download additional PDFs without approval.

Create or update data/visual_resources.json for the two HFE infographics and relevant official YouTube instructional video links. Store titles, verified URLs, relevant topics, applicable stages and display conditions. Do not download or embed media without permission. These resources supplement guidance and are not automatically treated as policy evidence.

B. Extraction completeness validation

Produce a structured completeness report comparing:

Expected versus extracted sections from the source-discovery matrix.

Accordion content and nested sections.

Source headings versus extracted headings.

Relevant links and unresolved linked dependencies.

Original tables versus extracted table values and structure.

Conditions, exceptions and applicant-category applicability.

Missing, duplicated or malformed passages.

Source/passage IDs and temporal metadata.

Where default and expanded HTML snapshots are available, compare them to identify content introduced only after expansion. Where only one snapshot exists, record that limitation rather than claiming equivalent validation.

Distinguish missing source content, extraction failures, unresolved linked sources and uncertain policy interpretations. Do not infer completeness solely from successful parsing or matching character counts.

Produce machine-readable completeness results and a concise human-readable summary. Avoid printing substantial copyrighted source text into terminal output, Git-tracked reports or coding-agent logs.

C. Policy coverage validation

Evaluate the extracted material against the approved MVP scope and source-discovery matrix.

Maintain a policy coverage matrix mapping supported requirements to:

Authoritative source IDs and relevant sections.

Applicant categories and applicability conditions.

Exceptions and exclusions.

Known or unresolved effective dates.

Extraction and manual-review status.

Distinguish source coverage gaps, extraction gaps, temporal gaps and insufficient policy evidence. Retrieval failures should only be assessed once retrieval is implemented.

Flag unsupported or ambiguous policy areas for my review. Do not silently invent rules, infer eligibility outcomes or expand the MVP to accommodate newly discovered material.

Identify policy-critical facts and exceptions requiring manual validation against the original official sources. Provide a concise review checklist with source IDs and section references.

D. Reviewer-facing knowledge base and licensing

Keep original HTML, PDFs, extracted source text and source-derived indexes under data/private_corpus/, excluded from Git and Docker build contexts.

Construct data/policy_facts.jsonl as the canonical reviewer-facing knowledge base, using independently authored, source-attributed factual representations.

Each fact should have a stable ID, relevant conditions and exceptions, applicability metadata, source references, temporal metadata and validation status.

Verify that every fact ID resolves to a valid source record and official URL without requiring access to private snapshots or absolute local file paths.

Conduct an independent-authorship and rights review. Compare authored facts against the source material and flag copied wording, superficial paraphrasing or uncertain redistribution rights.

Do not assume that transforming source content into JSON grants redistribution permission, or that an automated similarity check establishes legal compliance.

Keep the reviewer-facing facts consistent with the verified source coverage. Do not create unsupported policy facts merely to fill gaps.

Ensure the application and primary evaluation will use the same policy_facts.jsonl and compatible retrieval schema. The private source corpus is for provenance and completeness auditing, not an additional runtime knowledge source.

E. Freeze, reproducibility and quality assurance

Freeze the approved corpus version, recording source hashes, capture dates, processing versions, fact counts, coverage status and known effective dates.

Ensure the reviewer-facing corpus can be loaded without data/private_corpus/, network acquisition scripts or undocumented local files.

Implement only the necessary offline preparation and validation scripts. Prefer reusing existing scripts/snapshots.py; introduce separate scripts only where responsibilities are genuinely distinct.

Add deterministic tests using independently authored HTML fixtures for nested sections, tables, links, duplicate content, missing sections and source-reference integrity.

Update the source manifest, coverage matrix, data documentation, requirements register, architecture notes and decisions log as necessary.

Report actual test results and unresolved limitations. Do not claim source or policy completeness without the required evidence.

F. Final corpus and scope review

Recommend the final supported policy scope based on verified source coverage.

Identify unsupported, ambiguous, outdated or insufficiently evidenced rules and exceptions.

If extraction or validation becomes disproportionately difficult, recommend a smaller defensible scope rather than sacrificing correctness.

Deliverables

Offline extraction and validation pipeline.

Frozen source and passage metadata.

Extraction-completeness report.

Policy coverage matrix.

Rights-reviewed data/policy_facts.jsonl.

data/visual_resources.json.

Corpus hashes and version metadata.

Automated tests and actual results.

Licensing and reproducibility limitations.

Final supported-scope recommendation.

Approval checkpoint

Present the final corpus coverage, outstanding issues and recommended MVP scope for my review.

Do not proceed to the policy-rule registry or benchmark creation until I approve the corpus and supported scope.

Do not commit or push without my approval.

## 2. Dataset A — source acquisition and reviewer-facing KB [APP p.4–5, 11–14]

### 2.1 Two corpora (APPROVED, D-005)
- **Private source corpus:**
  - the original HDB HTML pages and approved linked resources;
  - kept locally for provenance, extraction and policy-completeness validation;
  - full snapshots and extracted copied-text passages are **excluded from Git**
    (REQ-LIC-010, REQ-LIC-011).
- **Reviewer-facing canonical KB:** `data/policy_facts.jsonl`, which holds
  **independently authored, source-attributed factual policy representations**. Each has
  passed manual validation and rights review (REQ-DAT-010).
- The application, BM25 index, Docker deployment and primary evaluation **all use the
  reviewer-facing corpus** (REQ-DAT-011).
- The private corpus is **not** needed for normal execution or reviewer evaluation
  (REQ-DAT-012).
- The matrix, snapshots and extraction reports support building and auditing the authored
  facts. They don't expand the MVP (REQ-SCP-007).

### 2.2 Same interface, no transfer of claims (APPROVED) [APP p.13], REQ-DAT-013
- Both corpora should be usable through the **same retrieval interface**.
- Document any coverage differences between them.
- **Never claim that results on one corpus apply to the other.**
- **OPEN (Q-11):** is any experiment planned on the private corpus? If not, the
  same-interface requirement only needs to hold structurally.

### 2.3 Source manifest — REQ-SRC-002 (APPROVED) [APP p.4, 14]
Required fields per source:
- URL;
- document title;
- access timestamp;
- source section;
- extraction method;
- **SHA-256 hash** of the snapshot, to show it didn't change between experiments;
- relevant policy scope [APP p.14].

### 2.4 Private passage record (APPROVED structure, private corpus only) [APP p.4–5]
- **REQ-SRC-003:** each passage keeps enough context to avoid misreading an exception. For
  example, a condition must not be separated from the heading that names its applicant group.
- Example fields from the source document:

  ```json
  {
    "passage_id": "HFE_001",
    "source_id": "HFE_APPLICATION",
    "section": "Application Requirements",
    "source_url": "https://www.hdb.gov.sg/...",
    "anchor": "#application-requirements",
    "content_type": "html",
    "retrieved_at": "2026-10-26",
    "policy_effective_date": null,
    "text": "Locally extracted source content",
    "review_status": "pending"
  }
  ```

- `text` holds copied source content, so these records live only under
  `data/private_corpus/processed/`.

### 2.5 `policy_facts.jsonl` schema — PROPOSED (D-023; finalise in architecture/corpus design)

One JSON object per line. Typed with Pydantic in code.

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `fact_id` | str, stable, e.g. `HFE-VALIDITY-001` | Referenced by rules, labels and citations. Never reused |
| `statement` | str | **Independently authored** factual paraphrase. No substantial copied text |
| `topic` | enum (e.g. `household`, `hfe`, `income_docs`, `application`, `non_selection`, `priority`) | Retrieval facets and coverage gate |
| `scope_tier` | enum `core` / `limited` / `context` | Links to the MVP tier |
| `applies_to` | object of conditions (e.g. `{"household_type": "first_timer_couple"}`) | Applicability |
| `exceptions` | list of `{description, fact_id?}` | Keeps exceptions attached |
| `source` | `{source_id, url, section, anchor}` | Resolves through `sources_manifest.json` |
| `private_passage_ids` | list[str] (optional) | Provenance only; never needed at runtime (D-006) |
| `retrieved_at` | date | Temporal metadata |
| `effective_from` / `effective_to` | date or null; plus `effective_date_note` | Known effective dates and ambiguity |
| `validation` | `{status: draft/verified/rejected, method, validated_at, notes}` | Manual validation |
| `rights_review` | `{status: pending/cleared, notes}` | Rights review before it is tracked |
| `kb_version` | str | Corpus versioning |
| `aliases` | list[str] | Synonyms and acronyms indexed with the statement for BM25 (e.g. "HFE letter", "fiancé"). **APPROVED addition (D-031)** |

### 2.6 Extraction (APPROVED) [APP p.11]
- **REQ-SRC-006:**
  - capture **only explicitly approved webpages**, by manual rendered-DOM extraction or
    controlled browser automation, subject to documented access and usage permissions;
  - preserve expanded informational sections;
  - **never** follow links automatically or interact with transactional services;
  - no automated discovery or unrestricted crawling [APP p.14].
- **REQ-SRC-007:** extract and normalise headings, paragraphs, tables, lists, links and
  document metadata.
- **As implemented (2026-10-28; D-055, D-056):** HDB's bot protection returns HTTP 403 to
  automated clients, so capture is **manual**. The "controlled browser automation" option
  isn't used, and its tooling (Playwright) was removed.
  - HTML pages: the developer saves the rendered DOM from a normal browser. All accordion
    panels were already in the DOM, so a single default-state copy per page sufficed.
  - PDFs: downloaded manually in the browser.
  - Files go to `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/<UTC>_<name>`.
  - Offline scripts: `scripts/snapshots.py audit` (completeness, structure-only output) and
    `scripts/snapshots.py register` (hashes and timestamps into
    `data/sources_manifest.json`).
  - Acquired so far: S01–S05 (HTML) and S07–S08 (PDF). See
    [data_sources.md §7](../data_sources.md).
- Media rules are in [02 §4](02_policy_sources.md#4-media-handling-decisions-approved-app-p1112-18).

**Simplifications versus the recommended structure, with reasons:**

| Recommended item | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| — | **Added `llm.py`** | Three modules (`generation`, `verification`, and extraction inside `generation`) share one client. A separate module is the single seam where tests inject a fake and where caching and token accounting live. Without it, `verification` would import from `generation` |
| `evaluation/baselines.py` | **Dropped** | D-030: configurations A–D are the same pipeline with stages switched off, so they live in `pipeline.py`. A separate baselines module would duplicate prompt logic and break "equivalent instructions" (D-003) |
| Separate retrieval-query file | **Dropped** | Retrieval recall@k uses each benchmark case's gold fact IDs. One labelled source, no duplication |
| `contracts.py`, `knowledge.py`, `rules.py`, `gate.py`, `profile.py`, `evidence.py`, `report.py`, `extraction.py` (D-030 layout) | **Merged** into `schemas.py`, `policy.py`, `retrieval.py`, `generation.py`, `pipeline.py` | Each was small. If `policy.py` grows past about 400 lines, split out `profile.py` (recorded as an allowed refactor, no new decision needed) |

**Boundary rules:**
- `schemas`, `policy`, `retrieval` and `pipeline`'s report assembly are pure: they never import
  `llm`.
- Only `generation` and `verification` call the `LLMClient` protocol, so tests inject a fake.
- `pipeline` is the only module that knows about configurations.
- `evaluation/` consumes `FinalGuidance` and saved predictions. It never reaches into stage
  internals, except through the component metrics.
- `scripts/` is never imported by `src/` or used by Docker (REQ-DAT-022).

## 5. Pydantic contracts (proposed; finalised with the Phase 2 facts schema, Q-22)

Field names are indicative. Enumerations that depend on verified policy (employment
categories, topics) are confirmed in Phase 2.

```python
# ---- shared enums -------------------------------------------------------------
class Tier(StrEnum): CORE="core"; LIMITED="limited"; CONTEXT="context"; EXCLUDED="excluded"

class Topic(StrEnum):
    # in scope (tier fixed by D-008)
    HOUSEHOLD_COMPOSITION="household_composition"          # core
    APPLICATION_REQUIREMENTS="application_requirements"    # core
    HFE_PROCESS="hfe_process"                              # core (prerequisites, timing, validity)
    HFE_DOCUMENTS="hfe_documents"                          # core (incl. income/employment docs, D-013)
    PRIORITY_CONSIDERATIONS="priority_considerations"      # limited
    NON_SELECTION="non_selection"                          # limited
    HFE_GRANT_LOAN_CONTEXT="hfe_grant_loan_context"        # context only
    # excluded (D-008)
    GRANT_LOAN_CALCULATION="grant_loan_calculation"
    FINANCING_AFFORDABILITY="financing_affordability"
    BALLOT_ODDS="ballot_odds"
    POST_PURCHASE="post_purchase"
    ELIGIBILITY_DETERMINATION="eligibility_determination"
    OTHER_HOUSING="other_housing"                          # resale, rental, EC, etc.
    UNRELATED="unrelated"

TOPIC_TIER: dict[Topic, Tier]   # single source of truth for the gate, unit-tested

class ProfileField(StrEnum):    # addressable fields, for missing/conflict reporting
    RELATIONSHIP="relationship"; A1_AGE="applicant_1.age"; A2_AGE="applicant_2.age"
    A1_CITIZENSHIP="applicant_1.citizenship"; A2_CITIZENSHIP="applicant_2.citizenship"
    A1_PRIOR_HOUSING="applicant_1.prior_flat_or_subsidy"; A2_PRIOR_HOUSING="applicant_2.prior_flat_or_subsidy"
    A1_EMPLOYMENT="applicant_1.employment"; A2_EMPLOYMENT="applicant_2.employment"
    HFE_STATUS="hfe_status"; HFE_ISSUE_DATE="hfe_issue_date"
    PRIVATE_PROPERTY="private_property_interest"; HOUSING_LOAN_INTENT="housing_loan_intent"
    CHILDREN="children_or_expecting"

# ---- request / profile ------------------------------------------------------------
class UserRequest(BaseModel):
    request_id: str
    situation_text: str          # free text; fictional profiles only (UI warns)
    question: str

class Person(BaseModel):
    age: int | None = Field(None, ge=0, le=120)
    citizenship: Literal["SC", "SPR", "non_resident"] | None = None
    prior_flat_or_subsidy: bool | None = None      # drives first-timer status
    employment: Literal["employed", "self_employed", "not_working", "other"] | None = None  # Phase 2 aligns with HFE guide

class ApplicantProfile(BaseModel):
    """None = not provided. Never defaulted (REQ-ARC-013)."""
    relationship: Literal["married", "engaged", "other"] | None = None
    applicant_1: Person = Person()
    applicant_2: Person = Person()
    hfe_status: Literal["not_started", "preliminary_done", "applied", "issued"] | None = None
    hfe_issue_date: date | None = None
    private_property_interest: bool | None = None
    housing_loan_intent: Literal["hdb", "financial_institution", "undecided"] | None = None
    children_or_expecting: bool | None = None

class FieldQuote(BaseModel):
    field: ProfileField
    quote: str                    # verbatim span from situation_text

class StatedContradiction(BaseModel):
    field: ProfileField
    quotes: list[str] = Field(min_length=2)

class ProfileExtraction(BaseModel):            # LLM #1 output (schema-constrained)
    profile: ApplicantProfile
    quotes: list[FieldQuote]
    stated_contradictions: list[StatedContradiction]
    question_topics: list[Topic] = Field(min_length=1)

# ---- the four distinct signals -------------------------------------------------------
class MissingProfileField(BaseModel):
    field: ProfileField
    needed_for: list[str]         # topic values and/or rule_ids
    follow_up_question: str       # from a static template map (deterministic)

class ProfileConflict(BaseModel):
    fields: list[ProfileField]
    kind: Literal["stated_contradiction", "logical_inconsistency"]
    detail: str                   # e.g. "engaged, but described as spouse"
    quotes: list[str]
    clarification_question: str

class EvidenceGap(BaseModel):
    topic: Topic | None
    claim_id: str | None = None
    kind: Literal["no_evidence_for_topic", "claim_uncited", "claim_unsupported", "fact_temporally_uncertain"]
    detail: str
    official_source_url: str | None = None      # where to confirm

class OutOfScopeReason(BaseModel):
    code: Literal["excluded_topic", "unsupported_household_type", "unrecognised_question"]
    topic: Topic | None = None
    detail: str
    redirect_url: str | None = None             # official service/page

class ProfileAssessment(BaseModel):
    profile: ApplicantProfile                   # after quote guard
    missing_profile_fields: list[MissingProfileField]
    profile_conflicts: list[ProfileConflict]
    extraction_warnings: list[str]              # dropped unquoted fields, etc.

# ---- gate --------------------------------------------------------------------------
class CoverageDecision(BaseModel):
    status: Literal["in_scope", "partially_in_scope", "out_of_scope"]
    supported_topics: list[Topic]
    out_of_scope_reasons: list[OutOfScopeReason]

# ---- knowledge, rules, evidence --------------------------------------------------------
class PolicyFact(BaseModel):     # per 03 §2.5 (+ aliases, A2); loaded, never LLM-produced
    fact_id: str; statement: str; topic: Topic; scope_tier: Tier
    aliases: list[str] = []
    applies_to: dict[str, str] = {}; exce

**Tool call: Bash** — Print tag skeleton of S01 main content

```
cd "<repo>" && cat > <tmp>/b764a348-0454-427c-92e3-8af4cd9828e5/scratchpad/skel.py <<'EOF'
import sys
from html.parser import HTMLParser
VOID={"br","img","hr","input","meta","link","source","wbr","area","col","path","circle","rect","line","polygon","use"}
class P(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(s):
        super().__init__(); s.stack=[]; s.inmain=False; s.out=[]
    def handle_starttag(s,t,a):
        a=dict(a)
        if t=="main": s.inmain=True
        if t in VOID: 
            if s.inmain and t=="img": s.out.append("  "*len(s.stack)+"img")
            return
        s.stack.append(t)
        if s.inmain and t not in ("span","svg","path","g","strong","em","b","i"):
            cls=(a.get("class") or "")[:60]
            extra=" ".join(f"{k}={a[k][:30]}" for k in ("id","aria-expanded","data-testid","role","href") if a.get(k))
            s.out.append("  "*len(s.stack)+f"{t} .{cls} {extra}")
    def handle_endtag(s,t):
        if t in VOID: return
        while s.stack:
            x=s.stack.pop()
            if x==t: break
        if t=="main": s.inmain=False
p=P(); p.feed(open(sys.argv[1],encoding="utf-8").read())
print("\n".join(p.out[: int(sys.argv[2])]))
print(len(p.out))
EOF

1:\n        errors.append(f\"mixed kb_version values: {sorted(versions)}\")\n    for f in facts:\n        src = sources.get(f.source.source_id)\n        if src is None:\n errors\n\n\ndef load_kb(\n    facts_path: Path = FACTS_PATH, manifest_path: Path = MANIFEST_PATH\n) -> KnowledgeBase:\n    facts = load_facts(facts_path)\n    sources = load_manifest(manifest_path)\n
